title: Modifying tobacco thermochemistry with S-KHCO 3 : atmosphere-dependent product redistribution and sensory implications
content: Controlling tobacco pyrolysis-product distributions offers a potential route to improving sensory quality, yet the effects of additive loading and reaction atmosphere remain difficult to reconcile with sensory performance. Here, synthesized potassium bicarbonate (S-KHCO3) was incorporated into reconstituted tobacco sheets at loadings of 0–2.0 wt%. The resulting thermal products were characterized by pyrolysis-gas chromatography/mass spectrometry at 370 °C under He and air, and sensory performance was evaluated across six attributes. Structural and spectroscopic characterization identified potassium bicarbonate as the predominant crystalline phase of the prepared additive. S-KHCO3 modified the relative distributions of oxygen-containing heterocycles, aldehydes, ketones, nitrogen-containing heterocycles, phenols, carboxylic acids, and esters. Tentatively assigned compounds exhibited different loading responses under the two atmospheres, indicating selective redistribution within the detected product mixture. The 1.0 wt% formulation achieved the highest mean total sensory score, increasing from 82.25 ± 2.63 for the untreated sample to 91.25 ± 0.96 on a 100-point scale across four assessors. Further increases in loading reduced the mean sensory score, indicating that sensory performance did not improve continuously with additive addition. Together, these findings identify an intermediate loading associated with favorable sensory performance and establish atmosphere-dependent product redistribution as a central feature of S-KHCO3-regulated tobacco thermochemistry. This study provides a basis for integrating chemical profiling with sensory assessment when selecting tobacco additive formulations.
